title: Map the interview loop before studying
guidance: Confirm the round types, expected tools, and whether any preparation material was supplied.
Allocate practice to the weakest high-impact round instead of treating every topic equally.
whyItMatters: Preparation becomes a set of decisions tied to the actual format rather than an endless syllabus.
avoid: Assuming every company uses the same loop.
Collecting material without scheduling practice.

title: Practice observable behaviors
guidance: Rehearse clarifying, explaining a tradeoff, testing, and recovering—not just arriving at answers.
Use short timed simulations to expose where your process becomes unclear.
whyItMatters: Interviewers can only evaluate the reasoning and communication they can observe.
avoid: Memorizing polished solutions.
Mistaking passive reading for interview practice.

title: Remove preventable logistics risk
guidance: Confirm the schedule and time zone from the invitation.
Test the link, audio, video, power, and coding environment before the interview window.
whyItMatters: A stable setup protects attention for the interview itself.
avoid: Opening the interview link for the first time at start time.
Installing required tools immediately before the call.

title: Stage only useful materials
guidance: Keep the interview link, a blank page, water, and any explicitly permitted reference material easy to reach.
Close notifications and unrelated tabs.
whyItMatters: A simple workspace reduces searching and accidental distraction.
avoid: Building a dense cheat sheet you cannot navigate.
Using references the interview format does not permit.

title: Frame the problem before optimizing
guidance: Restate the task and clarify inputs, outputs, constraints, and edge cases.
Walk through a small example and identify a correct baseline before choosing an optimization.
whyItMatters: A shared problem definition prevents elegant work on the wrong problem.
avoid: Jumping from prompt to code.
Dismissing a brute-force baseline without using it to reason.

title: Implement in verifiable increments
guidance: Name the invariant or data structure before writing the critical loop.
Compile or mentally execute small pieces, then test normal, boundary, and adversarial cases.
whyItMatters: Incremental verification makes bugs easier to localize and explain.
avoid: Writing the entire solution silently.
Testing only the example from the prompt.

title: Connect complexity to constraints
guidance: State time and space costs using the input variables you defined.
Explain why those costs are acceptable—or what would need to change at a different scale.
whyItMatters: Complexity is useful when it informs a design decision, not when recited as a label.
avoid: Giving complexity without defining variables.
Optimizing a constraint that was never present.

title: Keep the design conversation sequenced
guidance: Clarify requirements and scale assumptions before selecting components.
Sketch one end-to-end read or write path, then deep-dive on the highest-risk area.
whyItMatters: A sequence keeps the discussion coherent while leaving room to revisit assumptions.
avoid: Listing technologies before defining the workload.
Deep-diving every component equally.

title: Make tradeoffs requirement-relative
guidance: Compare options against latency, durability, availability, consistency, cost, and operating complexity that matter here.
State when a different assumption would change your choice.
whyItMatters: System design has defensible options, not one context-free correct diagram.
avoid: Declaring a universal architecture.
Adding components without explaining what they solve.

title: Start with product behavior, not a model
guidance: Define the product objective, prediction target, decision point, and baseline.
Name offline, online, and guardrail metrics without inventing performance numbers.
whyItMatters: The model is only useful inside a measurable product and decision system.
avoid: Choosing a model family before defining the target.
Treating one offline metric as the product goal.

title: Design the full learning lifecycle
guidance: Cover data collection, labels, leakage risk, training, evaluation, serving, and monitoring.
Explain how feedback arrives and what triggers retraining or rollback.
whyItMatters: Many ML failures appear at data and serving boundaries rather than inside the model architecture.
avoid: Ignoring train/serve consistency.
Treating deployment as the end of the system.

title: Select the closest truthful story
guidance: Choose an experience with a real decision and enough personal ownership to answer the prompt.
State briefly why it is relevant if the match is not exact.
whyItMatters: A truthful adjacent example is more useful than a fabricated perfect match.
avoid: Forcing the same story into every prompt.
Inventing scale, conflict, or ownership.

title: Use STAR as scaffolding
guidance: Compress situation and task so most of the answer can cover actions, decisions, and results.
Add reflection when it shows a genuine change in judgment.
whyItMatters: Structure helps the listener follow the evidence without turning the answer into a script.
avoid: Reciting labels aloud mechanically.
Spending most of the answer on background.

title: Narrate decisions, not every thought
guidance: Pause to organize, then explain the question you are resolving and the evidence you are using.
Use short checkpoints so the interviewer can redirect the level of detail.
whyItMatters: Useful narration keeps the interviewer oriented without filling every second.
avoid: Continuous unfiltered monologue.
Long silent implementation with no checkpoints.

title: Signal assumptions explicitly
guidance: Name an assumption and why it is reasonable before using it.
Invite correction when the assumption materially changes the solution.
whyItMatters: Visible assumptions make reasoning testable and easy to revise.
avoid: Hiding a guess inside the solution.
Asking permission for every minor choice.

title: Treat hints as collaboration
guidance: Acknowledge the hint, restate what it changes, and incorporate it into the next step.
If it conflicts with your current model, explain the mismatch briefly and update.
whyItMatters: Responding constructively shows adaptability and preserves momentum.
avoid: Defending the old path after new information.
Pretending you had already reached the hinted idea.

title: Recover in a coding round
guidance: Restate what is known, shrink to a smaller example, and write a correct baseline.
Ask one precise clarification if a constraint is blocking the next choice.
whyItMatters: A concrete smaller step reveals structure and gives the interviewer something useful to evaluate.
avoid: Cycling silently through unrelated ideas.
Requesting a solution-sized hint.

title: Recover in a design round
guidance: Return to the primary requirement and trace the main read or write path.
State one explicit assumption and choose one bottleneck to examine.
whyItMatters: Requirements provide a stable anchor when the component space feels too large.
avoid: Adding more boxes to create motion.
Changing several assumptions at once.

title: Recover in a behavioral round
guidance: Take a moment and choose the closest relevant experience you genuinely had.
State why the example is relevant, then answer the core behavior being tested.
whyItMatters: Truthful recovery protects credibility and often produces a more specific answer.
avoid: Inventing an experience.
Apologizing repeatedly for needing a pause.

title: Use closing questions to understand the work
guidance: Ask about decisions, collaboration, engineering constraints, or what success in the role requires.
Build on context already shared rather than reading a generic list.
whyItMatters: Focused questions help both sides evaluate the working relationship.
avoid: Asking for information readily available in supplied material.
Turning every question into a performance.

title: Close the active problem cleanly
guidance: Summarize the solution, the most important tradeoff, and any remaining risk if time permits.
Correct a discovered mistake directly rather than hiding it in the summary.
whyItMatters: A concise close shows whether you understand the shape and limits of your own work.
avoid: Introducing a new architecture at the end.
Claiming completion when important cases remain.

title: Capture preparation evidence while fresh
guidance: Record the topics, moments of confusion, and process gaps that would improve future practice.
Keep confidential or proprietary interview material out of public notes.
whyItMatters: A short factual review converts the interview into a better preparation plan.
avoid: Publishing detailed confidential questions.
Scoring yourself entirely by interviewer reactions.

title: Follow up concisely when appropriate
guidance: Thank the relevant contact, mention one genuine point from the conversation, and keep the note brief.
Use the communication channel and expectations already provided.
whyItMatters: A concise follow-up can reinforce professionalism without trying to relitigate the interview.
avoid: Sending repeated status requests without new context.
Adding a long correction essay.
